answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to forge a costly, verifiable work history before it can transact: agents must complete attested tasks over time, and reputation is a lantern that only grows brighter with completed work, not new accounts. A mirror check compares claimed history against the public ledger, so a flood of fresh identities shows up as empty mirrors with no past. One credible identity costs weeks of useful work; thousands cost thousands of times that, making fake-identity attacks economically pointless while honest newcomers still join by doing real work.
